Report it as unknown. Don't guess a date, and keep it out of the totals.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `eos_status` | `UNKNOWN`, with a note such as "No published EOS date for <engine> <version>", the doc URL you checked, and the date you checked it |
| `eos_date` | Blank or `N/A`. Don't borrow a date from a nearby version. |
| `urgency` | `UNKNOWN` or "Needs verification". Don't rank it as low, medium or high. |
| Cost columns (current, extended-support, projected) | `N/A` or blank, never `$0`. `$0` says "confirmed no extended-support cost," which you haven't established. You can still show the current base cost if you know it, but leave the extended-support cost unfilled. |
| Totals | Leave it out of every EOS cost total. List it in a separate "Unverified / excluded" section with a count, such as "3 resources excluded: EOS date not published", so readers know the totals are incomplete. |

One check before you mark it unknown: some engines publish EOS per major version. RDS and Aurora, for example, list dates by major version, not by minor. If the docs set the date at the major-version level, using it is a lookup, not a guess. Cite that row and say in the note that the date comes from the major version.

If the docs don't support a date at all, the resource stays `UNKNOWN`. Add an action item to confirm the date with AWS (support case or account team) or to re-check the docs later.

without_skill.raw_output:
I didn't find any EOS report spec or skill in this workspace, so this is my recommended convention, not an established one. The core rule: don't guess the date and don't count the resource as $0. Mark it unknown, show it in the report, and keep it out of the totals.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `eos_status` | `UNKNOWN` (or `NO_PUBLISHED_DATE`), not `SUPPORTED`, not `PAST_EOS`, and not a date borrowed from a nearby version |
| `eos_date` | Empty/null. Never fill it in from the major version's calendar or a "typical lifecycle." |
| `urgency` | `UNKNOWN` / "Needs verification," a separate category outside the High/Medium/Low scale. Don't silently mark it Low. |
| Cost columns (Extended Support $/hr, monthly, annual) | `N/A`, not `0`. A zero reads as "verified no cost," which you haven't verified. Current on-demand/instance cost can still be shown if you have it. |
| Totals | Excluded from the Extended Support cost totals. List it in a separate "Unresolved / excluded" line with a count, e.g. "3 resources excluded, EOS date not published." |
| Notes column | Give the exact engine and version, where you looked (the RDS/Aurora/ElastiCache/EKS release calendar URL and the date you checked), and the next step: confirm with AWS Support or your TAM, or check `aws rds describe-db-engine-versions` for `SupportedEngineModes` and lifecycle fields. |

Why:
- **The totals stay defensible.** Every dollar in them traces to a published date and a published price.
- **Unknown cost is still visible.** A separate section keeps it from being mistaken for no cost.
- **Errors go the safe way.** A borrowed date can either invent a cost or hide a real one.

If someone needs a planning figure, add an optional worst-case column. It assumes Extended Support has already started at the Year 1–2 rate, and is clearly labelled "assumed, not in totals." Keep it out of the main totals.
